headline: This law gives the Department of Homeland Security's top management official more control over the department's vehicle fleets, with penalties for officials who don't follow fleet rules.
what_it_does: The law makes the DHS Under Secretary for Management responsible for overseeing vehicle fleets across the department and approving leases, purchases, and replacements. Each DHS component must submit a yearly vehicle allocation plan and fleet management plan, and the Under Secretary reviews them to keep fleets at an optimal, cost-effective size. The Inspector General must also review how these rules worked in fiscal year 2019 and report on their effects.

who_it_affects.group: DHS component agencies and their heads
who_it_affects.how: They must create yearly vehicle allocation tools and fleet management plans and send them to the Under Secretary for review.

who_it_affects.group: DHS officials who manage vehicle fleets
who_it_affects.how: They can lose annual performance pay if they do not follow the vehicle allocation and fleet management requirements in the prior fiscal year.

who_it_affects.group: Senior Executive Service officials whose offices have vehicles
who_it_affects.how: They can lose access to a car service if they do not follow the vehicle allocation and fleet management requirements in the prior fiscal year.

who_it_affects.group: DHS employees who use government vehicles for home-to-work travel
who_it_affects.how: The department must ensure its components follow federal and DHS rules on taking vehicles from home to work, which may affect how those vehicles are assigned and used.

when_it_takes_effect: The penalty provisions on leases, acquisitions, pay, and car service apply beginning with fiscal year 2019, and the Inspector General review covers fiscal year 2019.
